issue: Login session not persisted across page reload
actual: Registration works and auto-logs the user in (toast "Account created! Welcome to ThreadHive!" and nav shows username). However, the newly registered account's credentials cannot be used to log in afterward - attempting to sign in with the exact email/password just used to register returns "Invalid credentials. Try: tech@example.com", indicating registered accounts are not actually persisted for login. Additionally, after logging in successfully with the demo account (tech@example.com), reloading the page (navigating to http://localhost:7019/) reverts the header to show "Login"/"Register" links instead of the logged-in user, meaning login state is not maintained across a page reload.
evidence: Login attempt with just-registered credentials returned toast "Invalid credentials. Try: tech@example.com"; after successful login as TechExplorer, reload shows Login/Register links again.

Clicked Edit Profile, updated Bio to "QA automated tester exploring ThreadHive forum features." and Interests to "Testing, Automation, QA", clicked Save. Toast "Profile updated!" appeared and profile page immediately displayed the new bio paragraph and the three new interest tags (Testing, Automation, QA) replacing the old ones.

Selected category "General Discussion", entered title "QA Test Thread: Automated Forum Testing" and body content, clicked Create Thread. Toast "Thread created successfully!" appeared and navigated to /thread/thread-1788346560329 showing the correct category, title, content, author, and "less than a minute ago" timestamp.

Typed a reply and clicked Post Reply. Toast "Reply posted!" appeared, the thread's reply count updated from "0 replies" to "1 replies", the "Replies (0)" heading updated to "Replies (1)", and the new reply text "Great thread! This is a QA test reply." appeared immediately in the reply list with author and timestamp.

issue: No duplicate-submission protection on rapid repeated reply posts
actual: After typing the reply text "Great thread! This is a QA test reply." and rapidly clicking Post Reply 3 times in succession, the system posted the exact same reply content twice (visible as two separate identical reply entries with the same text, author, and timestamp), and showed 3 "Reply posted!" toast notifications. The reply count went from 1 to 2 with duplicate content, showing no deduplication or rate-limiting/duplicate-content guard is implemented.
evidence: Replies (2) list shows two entries both with paragraph text "Great thread! This is a QA test reply." posted by the same author within the same minute; 3 "Reply posted!" toasts appeared for 3 rapid clicks.

Clicking "Create Thread" with all fields empty showed warning toast "Please fill in all fields" and did not navigate/submit. Repeating with only Title filled (category and content still empty) produced the same warning and blocked submission, confirming the system validates required fields before allowing a post.

Clicked the upvote button on the thread itself: count went from "0" to "1" immediately and button became active/highlighted. Clicked the like button on a reply: its count went from "0" to "1" immediately as well. Both updates happened in real time without page reload.

issue: No edit functionality for published threads or replies
actual: Inspected the thread page (own newly-created thread and own replies) for any edit control. No "Edit" button, pencil icon, or menu exists on threads or replies - the only buttons present are the upvote/like buttons, "Back", and "Post Reply". Since users cannot edit a published post or reply at all, there is no way to trigger or observe an "Edited" mark or last-edit timestamp.
evidence: Enumerated all buttons on the thread page via DOM query; only vote buttons, Back, and Post Reply exist - no edit affordance found.

actual: The thread/reply composer is a plain HTML <textarea> with no formatting toolbar (no bold/link/list buttons). Posting content with markdown-style syntax "Testing **bold text**, a [link](https://example.com), and a list:\n- item one\n- item two" resulted in the raw text being displayed verbatim as plain text - the asterisks were not rendered as bold, the markdown link was not converted to a clickable hyperlink, and the list items were not rendered as a bulleted list.
evidence: Reply paragraph rendered as literal string: "Testing **bold text**, a [link](https://example.com), and a list: - item one - item two" with no HTML formatting applied.

Clicked the "WellnessWanderer" author link on a thread card from the homepage; navigated to /profile/user-4 showing the poster's public profile: display name, join date ("Joined almost 3 years ago"), reputation score (987), bio paragraph, interest tags (Yoga, Meditation, Nutrition, Travel), and their list of threads.

issue: Profile page only shows thread history, not reply history
actual: Navigated to own profile (TechExplorer, /profile/user-1). The page displays a "Threads by TechExplorer (3)" section listing all threads I created, but there is no section, tab, or list showing the replies I posted (I had posted 3 replies on the test thread: two duplicate replies and one markdown-test reply). Users therefore cannot view their entire posting AND reply history - only their thread-creation history is visible.
evidence: Profile page sections present: profile header (bio/interests) and "Threads by TechExplorer (3)". No "Replies" or "Recent Activity" section exists on the profile page.

Searched "keyboard" (title match) - only "Building a mechanical keyboard from scratch" thread returned, page header updated to "Showing results for \"keyboard\"". Searched "Pomodoro" (a term that only appears in the body of "Share your favorite productivity tips!", not the title) - correctly returned that single thread, confirming search matches both title and body content accurately.

Clicked "Technology (243)" category link; navigated to /category/tech showing heading "Technology" with description "Programming, gadgets, and tech news" and a filtered list containing only the 2 threads tagged Technology ("Building a mechanical keyboard from scratch" and "What programming language should I learn in 2024?"), excluding threads from other categories.

Clicked "Most Active" filter button; heading changed to "Most Active Discussions" and the thread list re-sorted by reply count in descending order (89, 67, 45, 41, 38, 34, 31, 23, 3 replies), confirming discussions are sorted by recent interaction/activity frequency.

Default homepage view "Trending Discussions" lists threads sorted by upvote/like count in descending order (156, 124, 92, 89, 78, 67, 56, 47, 1), and the "Most Active" view sorts by reply count descending. Both confirm the homepage displays popular/active discussions sorted by likes/replies/activity level.

After logout (banner reverted to Login/Register) and re-login with tech@example.com, nav restored "TechExplorer TechExplorer" identity. Profile page /profile/user-1 correctly displayed the FT-2-edited bio ("QA automated tester exploring ThreadHive forum features.") and interest tags (Testing, Automation, QA). "Threads by TechExplorer (3)" included the FT-3 test thread with its upvote count "1" (from FT-5) and "3 replies" intact. All posting history and interaction data persisted correctly across the logout/login cycle.
